title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
statement_short: Given the head of a linked list, remove the n-th node from the end of the list and return its head in a single pass.
hint: Small list size (<= 30) allows single-pass removal using two pointers spaced n nodes apart.
why_not: Right: Two Pointers with a fast pointer offset by n steps locates the target node's predecessor in a single O(sz) pass with O(1) space. Not Stack: Pushing all nodes onto a stack allows popping n nodes to find the predecessor, but uses O(sz) extra memory. Not HashMap / Hash Set: Mapping node indices to references allows O(1) lookups but uses O(sz) auxiliary space. Not Linked List (Fast & Slow): Fast and slow cycle detection pointers advance at different speeds (1x vs 2x) rather than maintaining a fixed offset gap of n.
